title: Plan-lane fairness and overflow controller
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement a per-plan lane controller that enforces fair access across Free, Paid, and Enterprise customers while preserving high-priority capacity for enterprise plans. The controller should monotonically degrade lower-tier requests when plan units are exhausted and transparently route overflow to compatible model variants or regional spare capacity. This ticket covers the server-side routing policy, the lightweight quota aggregator, and a safe rollout path with observability and kill-switches.

Scope:
- Create a PlanLane Controller that maintains in-memory bucket summaries and exposes TTL-backed counters for each tenant plan class.
- Implement an overflow router strategy: prefer regional spare pool, then compatible lower-cost model variant, then best-effort enqueue with bounded wait.
- Integrate with existing rate-limiter and metrics endpoints (Prometheus labels and tracing).
- Provide a conservative default config for hosted API and knobs for Dedicated customers.

Out of scope: billing changes, UI console visuals (separate PM ticket), deep KMS or encryption work.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong guarantees vs latency: we choose bounded, predictable degradation rather than strict hard-deny to avoid spikes in observed 500s.
- Memory vs accuracy: use TTL'd in-memory counters with periodic sync to Redis for long-tail correlation; avoids per-request Redis roundtrips but accepts brief divergence.
- Preferring regional spare capacity increases cost but keeps latency SLOs for paid customers; fallback to lower-cost model variants is cheaper but adds output-quality variance.
acceptance_criteria: PlanLane Controller enforces per-plan unit limits and exposes per-plan metrics (consumed, remaining, last-reset)
Overflow router follows preference order: regional spare pool -> compatible model variant -> bounded enqueue -> informative rejection with suggested retry-after header
End-to-end tests simulating mixed traffic (50% Free, 30% Paid, 20% Enterprise) show Paid 99th latency <= 120ms under typical load and Free requests are degraded before Paid in constrained conditions
Prometheus dashboards and alert rule for plan imbalance (alert if Paid throttles > 1% for 10m)
Feature flagged rollout with kill-switch and gradual ramp to 100% traffic within 48 hours
